newsitem.title: switzerland: Six Red Cross staff members killed in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Six Red Cross staff members killed in Chechnya.

text.p: Six Western staff members of the International Committee of the Red Cross were murdered in their beds at a hospital compound in the breakaway Russian region of Chechnya on Tuesday, the Geneva-based agency said.
Spokesman Tony Burgener said the dead were two Norwegians, one Dutch, one Canadian, one Spaniard and one New Zealander.
He said the ICRC had frozen all its activities in Chechnya with immediate effect after the attack, the worst since the killing of three Swiss ICRC staff members in Burundi in June.

The six medical workers were murdered in their residence inside a Red Cross hospital compound at Novye Atagi, 17 km (11 miles) southwest of Chechnya's capital Grozny, at four a.m. local when they were sleeping, he said.
"We are strongly condemning this attack, which is a serious violation of international humanitarian law. The hospital was clearly marked with Red Cross signs all over it," Burgener said.
"It was an attack on their residence when they were sleeping at four a.m. this morning. It was an assassination," he said.
The remaining 14 Red Cross staff members at Novye Atagi would be evacuated on Tuesday, together with the six bodies, he said.

Russia's Itar-Tass news agency quoted Movladi Udugov, first deputy head of the separatist government of Chechnya as saying the incident, if confirmed, "would be a terrible link in a chain of provocations against the fragile peace process in Chechnya."
ICRC official Kim Gordon Bates said an investigation had started into the killings. "This was not a theft. These people were targeted," he told Reuters.

Both Moscow and Chechnya's separatist leaders are trying to keep the peace settlement on track in the region where tens of thousands of people have been killed in 21 months of fighting between Russian troops and the rebels.
